title: Technology Accelerators
coreMove: Judge a tool by whether it accelerates the concept, not by its novelty or status.
sourcePressure: The source treats technology as an amplifier of momentum, tied to disciplined adoption and the Hedgehog Concept, while rejecting fear-driven or prestige-driven technology frenzy.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version turns the chapter into anti-technology rhetoric or generic innovation advice.

exampleSpecs.audience: a lab owner already known for rapid retainer repairs
exampleSpecs.stakes: a 3D printer helps only if it accelerates the lab's existing promise instead of becoming a showpiece
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the owner rejects a showroom printer and buys the smaller unit only after timing how it cuts same-day retainer remakes inside the existing workflow
exampleSpecs.firstImage: clear resin dripping from a retainer model under violet curing light

exampleSpecs.audience: a herd manager with a proven fresh-cow protocol
exampleSpecs.stakes: sensor tags should speed early illness detection, not replace stockmanship the farm already relies on
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager compares sensor alerts against the existing fresh-cow notebook for two weeks before expanding, proving the tags accelerate a discipline already working
exampleSpecs.firstImage: yellow sensor tags clicking against a feed rail before sunrise

exampleSpecs.audience: an archivist whose concept is fast family-history access for local residents
exampleSpecs.stakes: OCR matters only if it shortens the path from a surname question to a usable record
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the archivist times one patron's search through handwritten deed indexes, then repeats it with OCR and approves only the pages that serve the access concept
exampleSpecs.firstImage: powdery deed books open under a foam cradle

exampleSpecs.audience: a dispatch director pitched a predictive heat-map system
exampleSpecs.stakes: a prestigious map could distract from the center's proven strength in call-triage speed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director asks the vendor to show seconds saved in triage handoff, not map beauty, and stops the purchase when the tool cannot move that measure
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a glowing heat map reflected in a dark dispatch console

exampleSpecs.audience: a gym owner whose concept is measurable skill progression for intermediate climbers
exampleSpecs.stakes: the app should deepen member progression instead of becoming a novelty leaderboard
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the owner hides global rankings and keeps only route-attempt notes after seeing which feature helps coaches move climbers through the skill ladder
exampleSpecs.firstImage: colored route tags snapped onto a plywood overhang

exampleSpecs.audience: a mill manager serving custom repair shops
exampleSpecs.stakes: a laser cutter accelerates precision patch work only if it supports the mill's best-at repair niche
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager lays rejected hand-cut patches beside laser-cut samples and approves the tool only after repair callbacks drop for the niche job
exampleSpecs.firstImage: white sailcloth triangles weighted under brass pattern slugs

skillTargets: test whether a tool accelerates an existing concept
separate disciplined adoption from technology frenzy
identify when technology exposes weak conceptual clarity

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one tool you want. Write the existing discipline it would accelerate and the one measure that should move within thirty days. If neither is clear, wait.

sourceAnchors.name: technology accelerators
sourceAnchors.detail: the source says technology amplifies a clear concept already in motion and cannot create greatness from weak people, weak truth, or weak strategy
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Technology accelerators deserve force only after the engine they amplify has already been named.
